answer: Proof of unique storage: each agent identity must hold its own 200 GB block of random data, an onyx slab derived from its address so no two identities can share it. At random moments the chain sends a pulse: a challenge naming random offsets, which must be answered within two seconds, too fast to fetch from elsewhere. A missed reply is an echo of fraud and freezes rewards. One honest agent pays a few dollars of disk a month; an attacker running 1,000 sybils must buy and keep online 200 TB.
